tags.source: 2026-09-02: the five banners are the first planted board objects and they are a form, like shield or staff.
tags.note: Grouped as a quality, not a form: a banner is not something you swing, so the form rules (an enchant must reach it, a rule must read 'banner attacks') do not apply. Same reclassification the 2-hander and exotic tags took 2026-08-27.

specialties.name: Berserker
specialties.intent: You gave up your guard and your grip on your gear for the biggest swing on the field, and you cannot afford to miss twice.
specialties.source: Hell-TCG Warrior/Beserker (settled; spelling corrected, keeps the name in the collision with Barbarian/Berserker)

specialties.name: Shieldbearer
specialties.intent: You are the piece of the line that does not move, and the enemy has to solve you before they solve anyone else.
specialties.source: Hell-TCG Warrior/Shieldbearer (settled)

specialties.name: Leader
specialties.intent: You fight with your eyes up: your own numbers are good, and everyone standing near you gets better ones.
specialties.source: Hell-TCG Warrior/Warleader (settled, renamed Leader)

specialties.name: Reaver
specialties.intent: Everyone on this hex is bleeding, including you; the fight is a race and you started with more blood to spend.

triggers.effect: apply 2 Bleed to yourself

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Barbarian/Reaver | 2026-08-17: a startOfBattle trigger with an ENEMY radius fires on nobody — the two sides do not deploy near each other. Rebuilt as an aura, which is checked continuously. | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: armor -1; dodge -5. Parked abilities: aura: AURA radius 2 — an enemy that ends its Activation inside gains 1 Bleed || onKill: remove all Bleed from yourself. | 2026-08-17: third stat surge +1 — the fight is a race and you take more swings in it.

specialties.name: Warchief
specialties.intent: You drive the warband forward by fear and by blood — everyone hits harder, everyone pays for it, and nobody argues.

triggers.effect: every ally within 3 hexes gains +1 Strength for the rest of the Battle

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Barbarian/Warchief | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: dodge -5. Parked abilities: onKill: every ally within 3 hexes loses 1 Weak.

specialties.name: Bloodrage
specialties.intent: Every corpse makes the next swing worse for someone; you are strongest in the last third of a battle that has gone badly.

triggers.effect: gain +1 Strength and +2 Crit for the rest of the Battle, stacking

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Barbarian/Berserker (renamed — collided with Warrior/Beserker; name taken from its own power Blood Rage) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -2; resist -1. Parked abilities: onAllyDeath: regain 1 Stamina and gain +5 Accuracy for the rest of the Battle. | 2026-08-17: third stat surge +1 — strongest in the last third of a battle — Surge is the stat that gets you there.

specialties.name: Champion
specialties.intent: You pick one enemy out of the mess and make the whole battle about the two of you.

triggers.effect: remove 5 Weak from yourself and heal 3

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Knight/Champion | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: dodge -5; health +2. | 2026-08-17: my trim ranked stats by rarity and dropped a class-PRIMARY stat to keep a rarer one. Restored; the cheapest stat on’s ladder (Accuracy, then Dodge) was dropped instead.

specialties.name: Guardian
specialties.intent: You give your own protection away and stand in the doorway; the enemy can go through you or go nowhere.

triggers.effect: you lose 1 Armor for the rest of the Battle; every ally within 3 hexes gains +1 Armor for the rest of the Battle

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Knight/Guardian | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: movement -1. Parked abilities: onAllyDamaged: if the ally is adjacent to you, reduce that damage by 1. | 2026-08-17: third stat luck +5 — hard to crit is what standing in a doorway actually means.

specialties.name: Crusader
specialties.intent: Every blow you land burns; you are what gets sent at the things that should not exist.

triggers.effect: your melee attacks apply 1 Burn, or 2 Burn against undead, demon or horror

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Knight/Crusader | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: dodge -5; health +2. | 2026-08-17: my trim ranked stats by rarity and dropped a class-PRIMARY stat to keep a rarer one. Restored; the cheapest stat on’s ladder (Accuracy, then Dodge) was dropped instead.

specialties.name: Bowmaster
specialties.intent: You plant your feet and the fight comes to you at your distance; the price of that reach is that you cannot keep the one hex of daylight everyone else lives on.

triggers.effect: your bow attacks gain +5 Accuracy

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Ranger/Bowmaster (item-slot dump rebuilt as Reach and a stand-still trigger) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -2; movement -1. | 2026-08-17: carried a condition the engine has no way to check (did-not-move / made-no-attack / moved-N-hexes). Condition removed and the effect reduced to match.

specialties.name: Winged Assassin
specialties.intent: You do not cross the ground, you cross the air above it. Whatever you touch bleeds, and anything that reaches you kills you.
specialties.source: Hell-TCG Ranger/Winged Assassin (onDamage Bleed kept; flight rebuilt as Movement and terrain-ignoring leaps) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -3; armor -1; dodge +10. Parked abilities: onKill: move up to 2 hexes immediately, ignoring difficult terrain. | 2026-08-17: Flight is a granted MOVEMENT ACTION (1 Movement per hex, passes over units and obstructions, takes nothing from the ground on the way, one click). Airwalk is a standing property covering only the hex you END your Turn on. Neither existed in the content. | 2026-08-20: flight is a granted movement POWER, never a property. Grants power.flight. The old "grants: [flight]" pointed at an id that never existed.

specialties.name: Wayfinder
specialties.intent: The Ranger who is fine once they close. Broken ground is free to you, and you are carrying enough to fight in it.

triggers.effect: Terrain that costs extra Movement to enter costs you nothing extra.

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Ranger/Wayfinder (pathfinding rebuilt as terrain immunity; melee lean kept) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: precision -1; strength +1; health +2. | 2026-08-17: +2 Strength / +3 Health / +2 Item Slots, no Precision loss. Strength is OFF-PRIMARY for a Ranger, so it has to be granted in quantity to be worth anything — that is what makes this the hybrid melee branch. The ally clause on the terrain trigger was too complicated and is cut.

specialties.name: Sentinel
specialties.intent: Really slow, and shooting from further away than anyone else on the field. You pick your hex once and the battle comes to you.
specialties.source: Hell-TCG Warden/Sentinel (onTakingDamage Poison kept; watchfulness rebuilt on Vision, which had no Hell-TCG equivalent) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: movement -1. Parked abilities: onActivationEnd: if you did not move this Turn, gain +1 Armor and +5 Accuracy until the end of your next Turn. | 2026-08-17: rebuilt. The old version wanted you stationary and armoured, which is a Warrior, not a Ranger. -2 Movement / +4 Health / +2 Reach / +1 Precision keeps the identity in the Ranger's own stats. Deliberately four stats with a negative — the negative IS the identity here. onTakingDamage trigger removed.

specialties.name: Trapper
specialties.intent: You do not fight the enemy, you fight the ground they are standing on, and they cannot see a single thing you have done to it.

triggers.effect: place one unseen trap on any hex within 3 hexes of your starting hex: the first enemy to enter it gains 2 Slow

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Warden/Trapper (whole-army Poison on entry rebuilt as placed, unseen, per-hex traps) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -1; vision +1. Parked abilities: onHit: an enemy standing in difficult terrain when you hit it gains 1 Weak. | 2026-08-20: "clean up that movement stuff." A one-Turn Movement loss is now the Slow status — apply N Slow. Fourteen entries said this two different ways and every one of them needed the engine to remember whose next Turn it was. Amount unchanged.

specialties.name: Protector
specialties.intent: You grow the battlefield a wall and stand behind it; nothing you do is fast, and everyone you are near is harder to kill than they were.

triggers.effect: AURA radius 1 — briars close in around you: every hex inside costs an enemy 1 extra Movement to enter.

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Warden/Protector (KEEPS the name in the Warden/Beast Protector collision; party-wide Resist rebuilt as a radius, powers drawn from Druid's nature line) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: precision -1; movement -1. Parked abilities: onAllyDamaged: if the ally is within 2 hexes of you or standing in difficult terrain, reduce that damage by 1. | 2026-08-17 off-primary pass: spirit +1 was off-primary for a Ranger; Resist does the warding job and is top of the ladder. | 2026-08-17 quality pass: replaced a placeholder aura with a distinct effect.

specialties.name: Magical Friend
specialties.intent: Something small and bright walks the field on your behalf: it heals what you cannot reach and you see through its eyes.

triggers.effect: summon your companion on any hex within 2 hexes of you. It is a summoned ally with its own stat block and its own AI, it has your Vision, and it does not attack

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Beast/Magical Friend (HoBaT has no pet system — gated on needsCapability rather than faked, and every power is written to measure from the companion's hex) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: strength -1; precision -1; health +2. | 2026-08-17 off-primary pass: two off-primaries at +1 was nothing; Magic doubled makes the branch real. | 2026-08-20: summoning is a feature we want — "we can summon something, it has an AI assigned to it, whether it is an enemy or a hero, and it has a stat block." The companion is the first thing that needs it, so it is written in those words now instead of as a bespoke pet. See engine/COMBAT-SEQUENCE.md #Summoning and rule.summon-order.

specialties.name: Feral
specialties.intent: You are the thing that closes the one hex of daylight, not the thing that keeps it; you run everything down and everything you touch bleeds.

triggers.effect: your claw and brawl attacks apply 1 Bleed

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Beast/Feral (no companion needed — the hero is the beast; claw is a real FORM tag so it carries the attacks) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: armor -1; precision -1; itemSlots -1; health +2. Parked abilities: onKill: move up to 2 hexes immediately.

specialties.name: Beastward
specialties.intent: You are what stands between the party and the things in the treeline, and you pay for every ally you keep upright out of your own body.

triggers.effect: you and every ally within 3 hexes gain +1 Resist for the rest of the Battle

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Beast/Protector (RENAMED — collided with Warden/Protector; rebuilt companion-free as a hero who wards the party against beast, horror and dragon) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: accuracy -5; movement -1. Parked abilities: onAllyDamaged: if the attacker is a beast, horror or dragon and the ally is within 3 hexes of you, reduce that damage by 2.

specialties.name: Poison Master
specialties.intent: You never win the exchange and you do not try to; you land one cut, you walk away, and you let the next four Turns do the killing.

triggers.effect: Immunity to Poison 3

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Rogue/Poison Master (its Poison Trap was already spent on Ranger's specialty.trapper — this line was rebuilt around a self-immunity and per-tick Resist arithmetic instead) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: strength -1; accuracy -5; health +1. Parked abilities: onHit: your dagger and thrown attacks apply 1 Poison; each tick of it is reduced separately by the target's Resist. | 2026-08-20: "you ignore all Poison applied to you from any source" is cut. Immunity N is the mechanic that already does this — it removes N before the status resolves — so this is Immunity to poison 3.

specialties.name: Assassin
specialties.intent: You spend the first half of a battle not existing, and the whole of it is arranged so that one enemy has an ally in front of it and you behind.

triggers.effect: you begin the Battle in stealth: you cannot be seen and cannot be targeted by an attack. Area effects, terrain and auras all still reach you. It breaks the moment you use an attack or a power, and whenever a reveal effect finds you — moving never breaks it

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Rogue/Assassin (name kept — no id collision with Ranger's specialty.winged-assassin, which Hell-TCG also ran alongside it; the onDamage hook rebuilt as flanking plus a stealth opener) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -3; armor -1; strength +1. Parked abilities: onHit: you are flanking when you and an ally are both adjacent to the target on two hexes that are not adjacent to each other; a flanking attack of yours gains +2 Strength || onHit: an attack made out of stealth gains +15 Crit; making it breaks stealth. | 2026-08-17: my trim ranked stats by rarity and dropped a class-PRIMARY stat to keep a rarer one. Restored; the cheapest stat on’s ladder (Accuracy, then Dodge) was dropped instead. | 2026-08-17 design pass: stealth rewritten to the settled definition: it breaks on an attack OR a power, never on movement, and the invented "breaks when you gain Burn" clause is gone.

specialties.name: Shadowdancer
specialties.intent: You are never where the swing lands, because you were never on that hex; the map has a hole in it and the hole is you.

triggers.effect: immediately enter stealth, then move up to 2 hexes. Movement never breaks stealth; only using an attack or a power does

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Rogue/ShadowDancer (spelling normalised; the +2 Reach was cut — Reach does nothing for a dagger — and the Dodge stack rebuilt around actually leaving the map) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -3; armor -1; strength -1; vision +1. Parked abilities: onActivationEnd: if you neither attacked nor used a power this Turn and no enemy is adjacent to you, enter stealth. | 2026-08-17 design pass: "move 2 hexes without breaking it" implied movement breaks stealth, which it never does — reworded so the branch reads the rule correctly.

specialties.name: Shadowbound
specialties.intent: You do not hide in the dark, you bring it with you, and everyone else has to fight at your Vision instead of theirs.

triggers.effect: your starting hex and every hex adjacent to it become darkness

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Ebony Mask/Shadowbound (Corruption is non-combat and was left there; the shadow magic rebuilt as terrain, which is the only thing that makes Vision bite) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -2; strength -1; precision -1; resist +1. Parked abilities: onKill: the hex the enemy fell on becomes darkness for the rest of the Battle || onTurnStart: while you stand in darkness you have +5 Dodge and +1 Resist. | 2026-08-17 off-primary pass: Magic doubled — the shadow-magic Rogue is a genuine hybrid, so it has to be paid for. | 2026-08-20: ground layers are PERSISTENT and carry no number and no clock. A hex is burning or it is not. One layer per hex; applying a different one replaces it. See rule.ground-layers.

specialties.name: Contractbound
specialties.intent: You signed something before the fight started, and it is drinking out of you for as long as the fight runs.

triggers.effect: you have +2 Strength and +5 Crit for the rest of the Battle, and you take 2 true damage at the start of each of your Turns

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Ebony Mask/Contractbound (Faith was CUT — 'kills earn faith, death costs it' rebuilt as a named mark you bleed for until you close it) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -2; resist -1; strength +1. Parked abilities: onKill: if the unit killed was your mark, heal 5, the debt ends, and you may name a new mark at the start of your next Turn. | 2026-08-17: my trim ranked stats by rarity and dropped a class-PRIMARY stat to keep a rarer one. Restored; the cheapest stat on’s ladder (Accuracy, then Dodge) was dropped instead. | 2026-08-20: the mark is cut. the named-enemy mark was a per-target designation system the engine does not have. The contract now simply runs on you: the bonus and the bill both apply from the start, no target to nominate.

specialties.name: Nightblade
specialties.intent: You open a hole in someone and then stand back at knife-throwing distance while it empties; nothing you cut ever stops leaking.

triggers.effect: your dagger and thrown attacks apply 2 Bleed. Bleed is TRUE damage, so nothing mitigates it

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Ebony Mask/Nightblade ('every cut bleeds' kept literally; the Reach kept and paid for in Health, since Reach is the one stat that makes thrown daggers a build) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -3; armor -1; dodge -5; strength +1. Parked abilities: onActivationEnd: if no enemy is within 3 hexes of you, enter stealth. | 2026-08-17: my trim ranked stats by rarity and dropped a class-PRIMARY stat to keep a rarer one. Restored; the cheapest stat on’s ladder (Accuracy, then Dodge) was dropped instead.

specialties.name: Havoc
specialties.intent: You close the whole field in one motion and leave a line of things bleeding out behind you; standing still is how you die.

triggers.effect: your melee attacks apply 2 Bleed, or 4 Bleed against demon and undead; Bleed is flat and is never reduced by Resist

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Demon Hunter/Havoc (bleeding-on-attack kept; the row-wipe rebuilt as movement plus a slayer band on demon and undead) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: armor -1; health -1; accuracy -5; strength +1. Parked abilities: onKill: regain 1 Stamina and move up to 2 hexes immediately. | 2026-08-17: my trim ranked stats by rarity and dropped a class-PRIMARY stat to keep a rarer one. Restored; the cheapest stat on’s ladder (Accuracy, then Dodge) was dropped instead.

specialties.name: Demonic Ward
specialties.intent: You are the one member of this class who is not hiding: you see the things that hide, you say where they are, and you are still standing when they reach you.

triggers.effect: AURA radius 2 — you and every ally inside have +1 Resist and see every demon and undead within your Vision through darkness and fog; any stealthed demon or undead within your Vision is revealed and its stealth breaks

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Demon Hunter/Demonic Ward (Protection and Burn-stripping kept; 'Spectral Sight' promoted from a Reach buff into the class's reveal, which is the counter to its own stealth line) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: movement -1; dodge -5; crit -2; vision +3. Parked abilities: onTakingDamage: if the attacker is a demon or undead, reduce that damage by 2. | 2026-08-17 design pass: the see-through-stealth half was a battle-start snapshot, which shows nothing at deployment; rebuilt as an aura, which is checked continuously, and written as a proper reveal.

specialties.name: Vengeance
specialties.intent: You are the Rogue who stands in the open and lets it happen, because every wound they open on you makes the next one you open on them worse.

triggers.effect: gain +1 Crit and +2 Accuracy for the rest of the Battle, stacking

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Demon Hunter/Vengeance (onTakingDamage kept as the whole identity; built on Crit and Accuracy, which had no Hell-TCG equivalent, so being hit sharpens you rather than just inflating damage) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: dodge -10; movement -1; health +4. Parked abilities: onKill: heal 3, or 6 if the unit was a demon or undead. | 2026-08-20: "if the attacker is adjacent to you it gains 1 Bleed" read the attacker’s position. Cut.

specialties.name: Fire-master
specialties.intent: You do not aim at units, you aim at ground: the field burns where you point, and everyone has to walk around your work.

triggers.effect: your staff attacks apply 2 Burn

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Mage/Fire-master (row Burn rebuilt as burning-terrain painting; the +2 Reach became +1 Reach, which is worth more here) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -2; movement -1. Parked abilities: startOfBattle: burning hexes deal you no damage for the rest of the Battle; they still halve your healing and still reveal you in darkness. | 2026-08-20: "or 2 Burn if the target is standing on a burning hex" was a terrain check on the target’s hex. Flat 2.

specialties.name: Soul Stealer
specialties.intent: Every wound you open is a meal; you have almost no Health of your own and you take everyone else's.

triggers.effect: your staff attacks heal you 2

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Mage/Soul Stealer (the extra-wound clause cut; ranged 2 became Precision 2) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -3; luck -3. Parked abilities: onKill: heal 4 and gain +1 Magic for the rest of the Battle — remember Magic is the party-wide sum, so the whole party's spells improve. | 2026-08-17: third stat crit +3 — every wound you open is a meal, so you want to open the worst ones. | 2026-08-20: the burning-ground halving is cut — Burn does that on its own.

specialties.name: Mystic
specialties.intent: You see the fight one beat before it happens: you barely damage anything, and everyone standing near you stops missing.

triggers.effect: your staff attacks apply 2 Weak

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Mage/Mystic (kept; the seer half rebuilt on Vision, which Hell-TCG had no equivalent for) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -2; precision -1; vision +2. Parked abilities: startOfBattle: every ally within 3 hexes gains +5 Accuracy for the Battle; on an already-reliable hero that surplus becomes Crit at a quarter rate. | 2026-08-17 off-primary pass: a Mage with no Magic at all was the oddest block in the set.

specialties.name: Storm Caller
specialties.intent: You are the longest reach on the field and the thinnest skin: everything you throw jumps to a second target, and nothing survives touching you.

triggers.effect: your staff attacks deal +2 damage against a target carrying Frost

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Shaman/Storm Caller (kept; the +2 Reach halved because Reach is ranged-only and expensive here) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: armor -1; health -2. Parked abilities: onTakingDamage: the attacker gains 1 Stun the first time it hits you each Turn.

specialties.name: Totem Master
specialties.intent: You plant your feet and the ground around you becomes yours; the moment you move, every promise you made lapses.

triggers.effect: gain +1 Magic for the rest of the Battle, once

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Shaman/Totem Master (HoBaT has no summons — totems rebuilt as caster-centred auras that lapse the Turn you move, which preserves the turnEnd/onTakingDamage Magic ratchet exactly) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: movement -1; precision -1; dodge -5. Parked abilities: onTakingDamage: lose 1 of the Magic accumulated this way, to a minimum of 0. | 2026-08-17: carried a condition the engine has no way to check (did-not-move / made-no-attack / moved-N-hexes). Condition removed and the effect reduced to match.

specialties.name: Spirit Walker
specialties.intent: You are the party's second life: you mend what the fight takes, and you pay for it by making everyone's spells a little weaker.

triggers.effect: lay the cold thread on yourself or on one ally within 3 hexes: it gains 1 Frost, which cancels every point of Burn on it as it lands and amplifies the next physical damage it takes.

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Shaman/Spirit Walker (kept; the -1 Magic is new — a healer shaman dilutes the party-wide Magic sum, which is the real cost of taking one) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: magic -1; health +3. Parked abilities: startOfBattle: you may cross burning and frost hexes without taking their effects for the rest of the Battle. | 2026-08-17 off-primary pass: Spirit doubled — it is the branch identity. | 2026-08-17: CUT. ally-reactive hooks, guarding, Consequence-Stack interference and non-knockback forced movement all removed by ruling. | 2026-08-17 quality pass: replaced a placeholder aura with a distinct effect.

specialties.name: Blightcaller
specialties.intent: You do not kill things, you make them worse: everything near you is weaker, slower and rotting before your allies arrive.

triggers.effect: every enemy within 2 hexes gains 1 Weak

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Druid/Nature Warden — RENAMED. Its turnEnd row-Weak is intact, but 'Warden' is taken: gen/ranger.json holds the whole Hell-TCG Warden class (Sentinel, Trapper, Protector) plus an invented Beastward, so a second nature-facing 'Warden' would read as the same branch on the wrong class. | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: health -2; accuracy -5; movement -1. Parked abilities: onHit: your staff attacks apply 1 Weak in addition to their damage. | 2026-08-17 off-primary pass: Spirit dropped rather than doubled; this branch is Magic, not healing.

specialties.name: Wild Shaper
specialties.intent: You gave up half of what a caster is for teeth. You put the Weak on them yourself and then you hit the soft place you just made — nothing else in the game finds a wound this fast.

triggers.effect: your brawl attacks add the target's Weak to their damage. They READ it: the stacks stay on the target and keep working

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Druid/Wild Shaper (HoBaT has no shapeshift system — the forms are rebuilt as a stance and a claw attack, which is why this branch pays 1 Magic to the party sum) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: magic -1; precision -2; itemSlots -1. Parked abilities: onKill: heal 3 and gain +5 Dodge for the rest of the Battle. | 2026-08-17 design pass: gave the branch the brawl/Weak identity — its own Primal Roar hands out the Weak and its bare hands cash it in; the flat heal-2 moved out of the way for it. | 2026-08-20: "I believe I do want Bear Form, but let's take it out for now." Removed. It was the only power in the game that replaces your whole kit — your Claw becomes your only attack and your other powers stop existing — and nothing in the engine expresses that. The branch is deliberately left SHORT A POWER rather than backfilled, so putting Bear Form back is a restore and not an argument with something invented in the meantime.

specialties.name: Grove Keeper
specialties.intent: You are the reason a bad fight is survivable: you put out fires, you pull the poison out, and you never once threaten anybody.

triggers.effect: every ally within 3 hexes heals 4

specialties.source: Hell-TCG Druid/Grove Keeper (kept; Harmony and Sanctuary were spent on gen/ranger.json, so the cleanse became a specialty trigger and the ward is new) | 2026-08-17 trim: three stats, no negatives, one ability. Dropped stats: movement -1; precision -1; dodge -5. Parked abilities: onActivationEnd: remove 1 Burn and 1 Poison from every ally within 2 hexes — each removed tick is a tick Resist no longer has to eat. | 2026-08-17 off-primary pass: Spirit is the heal stat and this is the healer-Mage, so it wants +2.

specialties.name: War Priest
specialties.intent: You are the only priest who stands in the front rank: your damage is small, but it is true, and nothing the enemy wears makes it smaller.

triggers.effect: your melee attacks deal +2 true damage against undead or demon

powers.name: Ground layers
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. A hex carries at most one status, and applying a new one removes and replaces whatever was there — curse a burning hex to 1 Weak and the hex flips from Burn to Weak, it does not hold both. The single exception is Burn and Frost, which cancel one for one instead of replacing (rule.burn-frost-cancel): frost laid on a burning hex subtracts from it rather than swapping it. Ground layers are persistent — they carry no clock of their own. The four layers are: burning · frost · poisoned · darkness. Darkness as a layer is the localised kind a unit paints on the board — distinct from Darkness the battlefield condition, which covers the whole map. The night family (2026-09-02) is what made the distinction load-bearing: those units paint darkness in radii around themselves.
powers.intent: The ground is a state, not a countdown. Frost put out a fire because it took the hex, not because it cancelled anything.
powers.source: 2026-08-20: "Status effects on terrain are just persistent. No turn tracking, just it is burning or it is frost. The only thing that should replace a ground layer effect is if a different one is applied, it replaces the previous one. The ground can only have one effect on it, and that effect stays." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "All ground effects, remove and replace, except Burn and Frost which counter. So if i curse a ground to add 1 weak, but it had burn. It flips from Burn to Weak. So each ground tile can only have 1 status on it." | 2026-09-02: the four layers enumerated on the row, darkness included.

powers.name: Summon order
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Every summoned unit is given a summon number when it arrives — the first thing summoned is 1, the second is 2, and so on, counted separately for each side. In its own Phase, summoned units activate FIRST, in summon-number order, BEFORE any unit that was already on the field. Summoned heroes go first in the Hero Phase; summoned enemies go first in the Enemy Phase.
powers.intent: A summon that arrives and then waits behind everything else is a summon that did nothing. Going first is most of what you paid for.
powers.source: 2026-08-20. Written ahead of the summoning system itself, which does not exist yet — see engine/COMBAT-SEQUENCE.md #Summoning. | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Enemy attacks are defined, and melee is the floor
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Every enemy states its attacks explicitly, by attack id — an enemy with no attack listed is unfinished content, not an enemy that cannot swing. If an enemy has no melee attack among them, it carries attack.basic.melee: Strength +0, melee reach, no stamina. A ranged enemy still has it, for when something closes.
powers.intent: Nothing on the board is ever unable to act. A caster shoved into melee swings for Strength; it does not stand there empty-handed.
powers.source: 2026-08-30: "every enemy needs its attacks clearly defined. If it does not have a melee attack, an enemy has a basic melee S+0 damage attack." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Nothing outlasts the Battle
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. No effect in the game persists past the end of the Battle — not a stat change, not a status, not a drain, not a scar. The longest any effect can last is the rest of the Battle, which is the first of the four durations. "Permanent" in any entry means permanent WITHIN the Battle and nothing more; an effect that would carry into the next Battle does not exist.
powers.intent: The Battle is the unit of consequence. A hero who ends one drained is whole at the start of the next, and content never has to reason about state it cannot see.
powers.source: 2026-08-31: "There's no permanent past the end of battle for anything." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: A status magnitude is a value
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Any status a unit is carrying may be read as a NUMBER by damage or by another effect — "Strength + 2 x the target's Root" is legal, and so is scaling a duration, a heal or a chance off a status the target already has. This holds for every status, not a named few.
powers.intent: It gives every status a second life. A debuff you applied three Phases ago is still worth something because the next attack reads it.
powers.source: 2026-09-01: "All of them or status effects can also be used to change the scale of damage or effect." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Forced movement is Knockback and Pull
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. There are exactly THREE forced-movement verbs: Knockback, which pushes a unit directly away from the source; Pull, which draws it directly toward the source; and DRIVE, which is a Knockback in which THE ATTACKER ALSO MOVES FORWARD — the target is pushed and the attacker advances into the hex it left. All three take a number of hexes and all three run on ONE axis: nothing moves sideways. No fourth verb.
powers.intent: Two opposed verbs, one axis. The 2026-08-20 cut left only Knockback because Pull had arrived as a bespoke system for one power; reinstated 2026-09-01 as a first-class verb with a real roster behind it.
powers.source: 2026-09-01: "Yep, I'm adding pull back in. It's a reversal." Reverses the 2026-08-20 ruling "the pull is cut. Knockback is the only forced movement in the game." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | 2026-09-01: the 'no third verb' clause is SUPERSEDED. Drive added, verbatim: 'Drive is knockback, but the attacker also moves forward.'

powers.name: Limits stop stacking; options need no limit
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. The per-unit limits on Armor, Idols, Blood Runes and Relics exist for ONE reason: to stop every item slot being additive in the same direction. A hero may not wear five defensive things. Trinkets carry no such limit because a trinket gives an OPTION — a thing you can do — not a bigger number, so five of them buy five choices rather than five stacks. The authoring test is therefore: if it is additive it belongs in a limited category; if it is an option it can be a trinket. The one deliberate exception is a status IMMUNITY, which is additive but conditional: it is often worth nothing, so its value is the pre-battle question of who should carry it today. That is a War Council decision, not a stack, and immunities stay trinkets.
powers.intent: It makes item slots a COVERAGE budget rather than a power budget. Handing a hero another slot makes them more flexible, not stronger — which is why slots can grow generously without inflating anything.
powers.source: 2026-09-02: "The reason for the Idol, Blood Rune / Armor / Relic limits are to prevent EVERY item slot from being additive in any direction. So I can't just add 5 defensive things. Because the Trinkets mostly give options, they don't need that limit." And on the exception: "I intentionally had immunities as an exception, because they are useless often, [I] want it in planning. OK, I can use my immunity — on whom? Is a good, non-permanent choice in battle prep." | Merged onto the trunk from the parallel chat 2026-09-02; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling.

powers.name: All healing comes from one function
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. There is ONE heal in the game and every source routes through it — a power, an item, a trigger, a lifesteal rider, and REGENERATION, which does not heal by a private path of its own but calls the same function at End of Phase. Anything that modifies healing therefore modifies all of it, once, in one place: Karma raises the amount, Burn halves it. Content never has to say which kinds of healing it means, because there is only one kind. THE STATIONS RUN IN ORDER: base -> all bonuses (Karma and any other) -> Burn halves -> applied to Health, and half the applied amount comes off Bleed. Regeneration calls this function like everything else, so a Regeneration tick is healed, halved and Bleed-stripping exactly as a cast heal is.
powers.intent: It turns three special cases into one pipeline. Karma boosting heals, Burn halving them and Regeneration ticking are not three rules that happen to touch health — they are stations on a single function, and a new modifier is written once instead of per source.
powers.source: 2026-09-02: "Regeneration should CAUSE healing, healing should all come from same function." Answers the open question from the healing-cures-Bleed decision: Regeneration IS healing received, so everything true of a heal is true of a Regeneration tick. | Merged onto the trunk from the parallel chat 2026-09-02; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling. | 2026-09-02, the station order ruled verbatim: 'karma and bonuses to healing before Burn, then halved, then applied'. This was the one thing rule.one-healing-function left open.
powers.stations: THE ORDER, ruled 2026-09-02: (1) the base heal; (2) ALL BONUSES TO HEALING, Karma included, are added; (3) Burn HALVES the result; (4) what remains is applied to Health — and half of that applied amount is removed from Bleed (rounded nearest, 0.5 up). Bonuses before the halving, always: Karma 3 on a Regeneration 4 tick with Burn present heals (4+3)/2 = 4 (rounds nearest, 0.5 up), and sheds 2 Bleed.

powers.name: Burn and Frost cancel
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. Burn and Frost annihilate each other one for one, at the moment either is applied — a unit never carries both. Apply 2 Burn to a unit holding 1 Frost and it ends on 1 Burn; apply 1 Frost to that unit and it ends on 0. The same cancellation is the ONE exception to ground layers replacing each other (rule.ground-layers).
powers.intent: Fire and ice are the only pair in the game that argue instead of taking turns.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "Do you have a note that Frost and Burn counter each other. Add 2 burn to a target with 1 Frost, you end up with 1 Burn. Add a frost to that unit and you end up with 0."

powers.name: Corpses
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. A CORPSE is a board object, and it is what every raise, summon, consume and feed in the game reads. Corpses are created when any enemy is DOWNED and when a hero actually DIES (the deathbed check fails, or the bleed-out clock runs out). FOUR THINGS DENY ONE, and denying a corpse is the counter to the whole undead economy: (1) DESTROY CORPSE — an on-kill effect, mostly a hero ability, that destroys the body as it falls; (2) SUMMONS NEVER LEAVE ONE, so a zombie raised from a corpse leaves nothing when it dies and the loop cannot feed itself; (3) OBLITERATION by Shadow reaching Max Health removes the unit with no corpse (status.shadow); (4) an effect that consumes corpses removes them outright. A denied corpse stops raising, stops summoning, stops the Escalating Demon, and stops anything else that feeds on bodies.
powers.intent: The undead do not have a damage problem, they have a supply problem. This is the supply.
powers.source: RULED: corpse creation 2026-08-25 ('Corpses are created by any enemy that gets downed and any hero that actually dies', with the bleed-out timer). DESTROY CORPSE and the summons clause were dictated 2026-08-30 (DESIGN-DUMP-CLEANED.md §9) and had never reached the pipeline — landed 2026-09-02 when it was asked for. Obliteration joins them from the same day's Shadow ruling. capability.corpses in gen/enemies-authored.json is the engine-side name for the board object.

powers.name: Stealth does not hold
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. At the End of every Phase there is a 25% chance that one random stealthed unit is revealed — either side, no condition. Stealth is therefore never safe and never certainly lost: it holds on average four Phases, and a battle in which nobody commits still runs out of hidden things.
powers.intent: You cannot win by waiting, and you cannot count on hiding.
powers.needsCapability: capability.stealth — designed in COMBAT-DESIGN (a stealth unit cannot be targeted and does not appear on the map), not yet built.
powers.source: Dictated 2026-09-02. REFRAMED at landing. Dictated as "if there are two full turns of no attack actions, one random stealth unit gets revealed" — which counts turns of history, and content is banned from occurrence counting and event history (R25). Ruled: rethink it. This is the history-free shape with the same intent — a per-Phase chance rather than a stall detector. It is strictly simpler and it also makes stealth a resource that burns. THE TRADE: it fires even in a busy battle, so stealth is temporary always rather than only when the battle stalls. Say so if the stall condition was the point. | 2026-09-02, softened by ruling: 'Give it a 25% chance that one random stealth unit is revealed at the end of every phase.' The certain per-Phase reveal was mine and too harsh — a 25% roll leaves stealth worth taking while still making it temporary. The roll needs its own named stream (Law 4), keyed by what the roll is.

enchants.source: Hell-TCG name reused (Bane Blade / Elemental Bane — the bane family, pointed at constructs) | 2026-08-17 quality pass: Armor shred floors out and left the enchant dead late. Knockback added on crit, so hammers, axes and chains have the effect their form implies. | 2026-08-20: the construct clause now also deals 4 true damage, which skips Armor and Resist both and so keeps paying after the shred has floored out. Knockback on crit stays.

enchants.name: Giant Slayer

triggers.effect: if the target is a giant, it gains 1 Slow

enchants.intent: You do not kill it. You hamstring it and make it walk to you, which takes a while and is the entire plan.
enchants.source: Hell-TCG name reused (Monster Slayer — split out onto the giant tag) | 2026-08-20: "clean up that movement stuff." A one-Turn Movement loss is now the Slow status — apply N Slow. Fourteen entries said this two different ways and every one of them needed the engine to remember whose next Turn it was. Amount unchanged.

enchants.name: Dragon Slayer

triggers.effect: if the target is a dragon, apply 3 Bleed

enchants.intent: Bleed is TRUE damage and a dragon is mostly Resist; the whole enchant is that one sentence.
enchants.source: Hell-TCG name reused (Dragon Slayer) | 2026-08-20: Bleed on hit raised 2 to 4, and the campaign Toughness grant became the Dragon Slayer badge, which is a thing that exists rather than a bespoke campaign rider. | 2026-08-20 sweep: the onKill line restated the grants field. The badge is awarded by grants: [badge.dragon-slayer]; saying it again in prose made it look like a bespoke in-battle award, which is the only one in the game.

enchants.name: Ghost Slayer

triggers.effect: every stealthed enemy on the battlefield is revealed and its stealth breaks

enchants.intent: Ghost was its own type in the old game; here it is two tags and a kill that turns the lights on everywhere at once.
enchants.source: Hell-TCG name reused (Ghost Slayer — the Ghost type folded into horror and nightmare) | 2026-08-20: Vision is not something an attacking weapon adds — cut. Slayer raised to +4 against both tags, and the kill now reveals every stealthed enemy on the map. NOTE: there is no tag.ghost; "ghost" was folded into horror and nightmare when this was first written, so +4 against ghosts means +4 against both of those.

enchants.name: Werewolf Bane

triggers.effect: this attack deals true damage against werewolf

enchants.intent: Silver does not hit harder. It hits past everything the thing was counting on.
enchants.source: Hell-TCG name reused (Werewolf Bane) | 2026-08-20 self-check: +fang. The Beast’s Claws could take this and its Fangs could not, purely because `claw` predated `fang`. Same weapon, same body, same enchant. | 2026-08-27: sword renamed blade in the workbook review — appliesToTags follows the rename (sword kept for any straggler rows).

enchants.name: Cursed Skull

triggers.effect: you take 1 true damage

enchants.intent: It talks. Everything it says is useful and none of it is free.
enchants.source: Hell-TCG name reused (Martyr, Cursed Skull — the party heal rebuilt as a Spirit line with a tithe) | 2026-08-20 self-check: +breath. Breath is the Beast’s magic-ranged form; the enchants that reach a staff reach it. | 2026-08-27: the wand and tome forms split off the staff tag in the review; they were staff-enchantable before the split, so the reach is preserved, not invented.

enchants.name: Tainted Blood

triggers.effect: Bleed on you ticks twice

enchants.intent: Six Health and a body that will not close a wound; you are bigger and you are leaking.
enchants.source: Hell-TCG name reused (Tainted Blood / Cursed Blood)

enchants.name: Martyr's Edge
enchants.intent: Two points on both damage stats is a tier-3 weapon's whole budget; this hands it to you and then removes the person holding it.
enchants.source: Hell-TCG name reused (Sacrifice) | 2026-08-19: power.beastward.sacrifice already owns "Sacrifice", and power.reaver.blood-price already owns the obvious replacement.

enchants.name: Blight

triggers.effect: gain 1 Corruption

enchants.intent: Toughness is injury capacity and the base for Deathbed Fighting, so this does not cost you damage — it costs you the campaign.
enchants.source: Hell-TCG name reused (Blight / Torment of Ire — rebuilt against Toughness and Corruption)

enchants.name: Riposte

triggers.effect: the attacker takes 5 true damage

enchants.intent: They swung, they missed, and the answer was already on its way. True damage, so their armour has nothing to say about it.
enchants.source: new 2026-08-20: the first counter-enchant on the onDodge hook. Thorns punishes being hit; this punishes missing.

enchants.name: Scalding Ward

triggers.effect: the attacker gains 3 Burn

enchants.intent: Step out of the way and leave the heat where you were standing.
enchants.source: new 2026-08-20: the status half of the onDodge counter pair.

enchants.name: Fire

triggers.effect: apply 1 Burn
apply 2 more Burn

enchants.intent: Burning arrows: a stack on every hit, and once every six Turns a patch of ground that burns on its own.
enchants.source: settled content | 2026-08-20: onCrit is a real hook now, and this is the standard rider on a status enchantment — a crit deals 2 more of whatever status it already applies. enchant.bloodletting had it first and it is now the pattern.

badges.note: THE CANONICAL CARRIER of the Destroy Corpse mechanic. The mechanic was dictated 2026-08-30 (DESIGN-DUMP-CLEANED.md §9) as 'mostly a hero ability' with no carrier ever named, so the verb had no user — and the effect vocabulary is a CENSUS OF USE, which is why nothing could author it. This badge is the first user and fixes the phrasing every later author copies: 'destroy the corpse'. NAME IS MINE, free to change.

classes.name: Warrior
classes.intent: The melee anchor. Armour is a mobility stat here — the Warrior is who finishes a run through threatened ground.
classes.bonusMoveNote: 2 stamina, 2 hexes, +2 Strength until end of Turn.

classes.name: Ranger
classes.intent: Standoff damage. Reach and Vision are its real stats and both are near-invisible, which is the design's own warning label.

classes.name: Rogue
classes.intent: Stealth, poison and bleed, daggers and thrown weapons. Arrives, strikes, and is gone before the answer lands.

classes.name: Mage
classes.intent: Magic damage and the terrain layer. Staves scale their basic attacks off Precision; only the big powers spend Magic.
classes.bonusMoveNote: 0 stamina, moves you ZERO hexes, gain 1 Stamina. A caught caster stays caught.

classes.name: Priest
classes.intent: True damage — it skips Armor and Resist both. Hits soft, hits reliably, and is the only thing standing between a fallen hero and the clock.
classes.bonusMoveNote: 0 stamina, moves you ZERO hexes, -1 Stamina Max for the Battle, gain 2 Stamina.

classes.name: Paladin
classes.intent: Armour, auras and protection, with slayer bonuses against undead and demon. The wall that also punishes.

classes.name: Civilian
classes.intent: An ordinary class, surfaced at different times. One action, no stamina bar, low-decision — three of them fill the flex slot one hero would.
classes.bonusMoveNote: No bonus move. The Civilian carries; it does not scramble.
classes.note: RULED 2026-08-27: "Civilians are exactly like heroes. They are another class of heroes. They shall all have 5 max stamina and 1 stamina regen. They need all of the same stats as heroes." The 0/0 baseline was wrong — struck.

classes.name: Beast
classes.intent: Teeth, hide and mass. The Beast is the mirror of the Civilian: it is granted NO Item Slots at any level, so nothing it does comes out of a bag — every point of it is the animal.

art.note: 19 assets per hero template, not per hero — which is why a generated hero costs no new art. 30 generative templates → 30 art sets.

sets.set: Hex map art — the battle-map token
Unconscious art — does NOT vary by level

art.rule: A status OVERRIDES the level band totally. A level-7 vampire shows vampire art, not tier-3 art. No merge.

rules.l1: Level 1 is the starting line, not a level-up. No class grants anything at L1.
rules.specialty: The specialty is chosen at the FIRST level-up — reaching level 2 — for every class. This resolves the dictated conflict: the Warrior dump said 'the first level up for a warrior, they choose their specialty', the Ranger table says L2 explicitly, and the class-power rule says 'at level two you choose a class specialty'. All three agree once 'first level-up' is read as the 1 to 2 transition.
rules.draft: Each power grant offers three: two from the specialty, one from the general pool.
rules.choiceLevel: Level 5 is the choice level for every class. One pick from the list, plus a small flat grant alongside it. Both dictated tables pair the choice with something flat, so all seven do.
rules.regen: Every class gains Stamina Regen exactly twice — once at L6, once at L10 — taking it 1 to 3. Civilian is the exception and gains it never.
rules.civilian: Civilian has no stamina bar, so it is granted no Stamina Max and no Stamina Regen at any level. Its power comes from Item Slots and gear instead — it ends with more slots than any other class. Now that Stamina Regen prices at 2.0, that exemption costs the Civilian 4.9 points across the run and it is the whole reason it totals 30.5 against the Warrior's 39.2.
rules.budget: Each row is priced on the stat ladder: Armor/Resist and Stamina Regen 2.0 · Magic/Spirit 1.5 · Strength/Precision 1.0 · Movement 0.7 · Item Slots 0.67 · Health/Reach 0.5 · Toughness 0.4 · Dodge 0.3 · Stamina Max 0.3 · Accuracy/Crit/Luck/Vision 0.2 · Surge 0.15. Rows run 2.2 to 6.5; the dictated Warrior's own ceiling is L7 at 6.40. Classes land 30 to 40 across the whole run.
rules.offLadder: Nothing is off the ladder any more. priced the last five 2026-08-20: Movement 0.7, Stamina Max 0.3, Stamina Regen 2.0, Surge 0.15, Toughness 0.4. Stamina Regen at 2.0 is the one that reshapes these tables — it is as expensive as Armor, every class gets exactly two, and Civilian gets none.
rules.movement: Movement is granted sparingly and never to a Mage or a Priest. Warrior L4 · Rogue L3 and L6 · Ranger L6 · Civilian L9 · Paladin L10, because armour should be the last thing that learns to run. Ruled by 2026-08-20. Beast L3 and L7 — two, like the Rogue, because a Beast that cannot close is not a Beast.
rules.itemSlots: Every class gains Item Slots across the run except the BEAST, which is granted none at any level. That is the branch: a Civilian is what it carries and a Beast is what it is. The ~4 ladder points the Beast forgoes in slots come back as Health, Strength and Reach.

classes.name: Warrior
classes.note: Every level grants +1 Health in addition to what is listed. The item-slot class: five slots across the run, more than anyone. Movement: +1 at level 4.

rows.note: Dictated as a bare list of five stat names — 'they definitely get a choice of a bunch of big things'. Magnitudes set to match the Ranger's dictated L5 list, which is the only place magnitudes were given.

classes.name: Ranger
classes.note: No per-level freebie — 'unlike Warrior, who got one health at every level, Rangers do not get that'. Reach is the Ranger's stat: four grants, twice anyone else. Movement: +1 at level 6.

rows.note: Dictated with magnitudes — the only L5 list that was.

classes.name: Rogue
classes.note: Crit and Dodge in volume — both price cheap on the ladder, which is exactly right for a class that wins by landing one hit and not being there for the answer. Ends at 27% crit, the highest in the game. Two Health grants total: the squishiest hero on the board. Movement: +1 at level 3 and 6.

rows.note: The single Resist grant of the run — a rogue with no Resist at all is free food for any mage, and this is the cheapest place to fix that.

classes.name: Mage
classes.note: Four Magic grants, rationed against the Warrior's four Strength — Magic prices at 1.5 because it scales off the party-wide sum. Precision matters too: staves scale their basic attacks off it. Never granted Armor at any level; the L5 choice is the only way a Mage gets any. Never gains Movement.

classes.name: Priest
classes.note: Accuracy at every single level and four Crit across the whole run — 'hits soft, hits reliably' written as numbers. Five Health grants and two Toughness make it the second-hardest thing to kill, which it has to be: it is the only class standing between a fallen hero and the clock. Never gains Movement.

rows.note: The Deathbed option is the only place on any table where a level grants Deathbed Fighting directly. Deathbed is derived, 20 + 5x Toughness, so this is a flat modifier hanging off the level row, exactly as a badge would.

classes.name: Paladin
classes.note: Three Armor and two Resist — five points of mitigation against the Warrior's two, and the reason every row is short. Armor and Resist are the two most expensive things on the ladder at 2.0, so the Paladin buys them by going without breadth: two Item Slots, one Dodge grant, four Crit. Health at every level from 2 upward is the Paladin's answer to the Warrior's freebie. Movement: +1 at level 10. Luck at 5, 7 and 9 for +5 total — the anti-crit stat on the class that is built to be hit.

classes.name: Civilian
classes.note: No Stamina Max and no Stamina Regen at any level — a civilian has no stamina bar, and that absence is the whole shape of the table. What it gets instead is Item Slots: six across the run, more than any other class. A civilian's power comes from what it is carrying, not from what it is. The widest L5 list in the game, ten options, because a civilian with no primary stats is defined by what it has been through. Movement: +1 at level 9.

rows.note: No Item Slot option, because the Beast never gets one. Reach is on the list instead — it is the stat that changes how a Beast plays.

derivation.accuracy: No source. Level-1 baseline by class: Priest and Ranger 80 (both are built to hit reliably), Rogue 78, Warrior and Mage 75, Paladin 72 (heavy and slow), Civilian 70 (untrained). Level rows add roughly +5 a level, so a level-10 hero lands near the 100 mark where surplus starts converting to Crit at ÷4.
derivation.crit: Base 3 — documented in the stat sheet. Rogue starts at 5, the only class whose identity is landing one.
derivation.luck: No source, and a rare grant in the level tables. Everyone starts at 0.
derivation.vision: Base radius 6 — documented. Ranger 8 and Rogue 7 and Mage 7, the three classes that trade on seeing first.
derivation.staminaMax: 5 at level 1 — documented. Civilian 0: a Civilian has no stamina bar.
derivation.staminaRegen: 1 at level 1 — documented, and it hard-caps at 3. Civilian 0.
derivation.surge: Not a baseline at all — Surge always EQUALS the character level. Documented rule, computed, never stored.
derivation.toughness: Ported, not derived: hell-tcg maxAfflictions IS injury capacity, which is what Toughness means here.

heroes.rule: ONE PIECE OF ART, ONE UNIQUE HERO. Ruled 2026-08-20. Every generative template owns four distinct designs and each is its own hero — so 12 Shadows subtypes are 48 heroes, not 12. What does NOT split is a hero’s own level-and-status set: a folder of 1/2/3/4 plus l/p/r/v is one hero at four levels wearing four afflictions, which is why the 98 fixed cast stay 98.

paths.note: the named cast. One hero per entry; their 1/2/3/4 + l/p/r/v art is levels and statuses, so they do not split
12 subtypes x 4 designs (-v1..v4) = 48 heroes sharing 12 stat blocks
12 subtypes x 4 designs = 47 heroes — sky-captain has only 3, its fourth file duplicates another
24 Eve base classes - one per piece of base art. Was 96: the four art files per set are four LEVELS, not four heroes
8 art templates (2 genders x 4 styles). Procedural: the art is fixed, the stat block is one draw

artConventions._note: What a filename suffix MEANS, per art directory. This exists because the same suffix means opposite things in different folders, and reading it wrong minted 106 heroes that were duplications of art — 72 in content/'s tutorial path, 29 in the Crucible's variants/, and 4 more from one subtype copied under a second name.
artConventions._theTrap: `-v2` means TWO DIFFERENT THINGS. In avtair-approved and aeronissa-concepts it is a fourth DESIGN — a different person sharing a subtype, and correctly its own hero. In the *-variants folders it is a rejected RETRY of one picture, and not a hero at all. Nothing in a filename tells you which; only the folder does. So the folder has to say.
artConventions._howItIsUsed: audit.mjs R22 collapses each hero's art filename to a CHARACTER STEM using the convention for its directory, then fails if two heroes land on the same stem. A directory with no entry here is itself a finding — a new art tree must declare what its suffixes mean before heroes can be built from it.

conventions.note: Same character-per-directory rule as card/. anim/ holds mp4, hex/ holds the board token at three sizes (_256, _1024, _full).

THE LOCAL TREE, and the one content points at. Unlike the hell-tcg folders it is unambiguous by construction: one directory per character, `l1`..`l4` are that character at four levels, and the four afflictions are spelled out in full - lycanthropy, possession, rotting-flesh, vampirism. There are no retries and no -vN here, because a rejected retry never gets copied across. Added 2026-08-22 when content stopped naming hell-tcg paths.
-v1..-v4 are four DIFFERENT PEOPLE sharing one subtype. Priestess of Ire v1-v4 are Sand Wraith, Blood Offerer, Snake Handler and Scorpion Keeper — four women, four heroes. Do not collapse.
Same as avtair, except the FIRST variant is the bare filename — there is no -v1 here.

One character per folder. -levelN is that character at four levels; -lycanthropy/-possessed/-rotting/-vampire are its four afflictions; -vN and -new are REJECTED RETRIES of a single picture. Which retry was adopted is ruled in crucible/data/art-rulings.json.

The flat root. `<class>-<style>1..4` is ONE hero at four levels and `<class>-<style>l/p/r/v` is that hero's four afflictions — this is the convention that produced 96 tutorial heroes where there were 24. Trailing digits and trailing l/p/r/v are NOT separate characters.
One bare filename per character. No levels, no afflictions, no variants.
Named *-series but does not follow the series shape — `void-dealer-1.png` is a bare one-off.

One FOLDER per character, and the filename is the slot: 1.png..4.png are four levels, l/p/r/v.png are four afflictions. The character is the folder, never the filename — every hero here would otherwise collapse onto a stem of `1`.
conventions._subtree: Matches below itself: every hero here lives in its own deep folder.

referents.name: the attacker
referents.means: whoever caused the damage that fired this trigger
referents.why: Hitting back at whoever hit you is what onTakingDamage is FOR. Ban 19 forbids reading the attacker's TAGS OR POSITION — conditioning on who they are — not striking them. Thorns N is the passive form of the same idea; this is the triggered form.

referents.name: the unit this hit
referents.means: the target of the attack this effect is riding on
referents.why: A rider on an attack acts on what the attack acted on. The source called this 'attacked'.

referents.name: the unit this missed
referents.means: the target of the attack this effect is riding on, when that attack missed
referents.why: The exact mirror of "the unit this hit", and needed for the same reason: a rider on an attack acts on what the attack was aimed at. Declared 2026-09-02 for the Dark Sniper’s Long Shot, whose whole design is that the miss still costs you. A spatial shape cannot say it, and on an enemy a raw source string reads backwards.

kits._note: Starting loadouts. RE-RULED 2026-08-27 (gear workbook review), superseding the 2026-08-25 shapes: every class draws from its startPool (the workbook's Start column). WARRIORS AND PALADINS draw TWO HANDS' WORTH — if the first draw is one-handed, draw again (a one-hander or a shield), NEVER THE SAME ITEM TWICE; a two-hander ends the draw. MAGES, PRIESTS AND ROGUES draw ONE weapon regardless of hands. RANGERS draw one bow. Weapons with no start pool exist to be found in game, never rolled at start. ARMOR: every classed hero also draws ONE random tier-0 armor from the armors whose startClasses cover their class (civilians and beasts draw none). Tier-0 armor costs no item slot — a dedicated armor slot exists, exactly one armor per unit. Draws are SPECS — the roll belongs to the draft (named stream), content stays deterministic. heroKits overrides replace the class draw entirely (e.g. the elven ranger will be assigned the Elfbow directly). Audit: R35.

class.warrior.why: Ruled 2026-08-27: two hands' worth — 1H first draw pulls a second 1H or shield, never the same twice.

class.paladin.why: Ruled 2026-08-27: same two-hands'-worth draw as the warrior, from the paladin pool.

class.ranger.why: Ruled 2026-08-27: one weapon from the ranger pool — no special bow rule needed, the pool IS all bows (Longbow included by ruling).

class.rogue.why: Ruled 2026-08-27: one weapon regardless of hands. Daggers (the new pair) included.

class.mage.why: Ruled 2026-08-27: one weapon regardless of hands — the wand, the tome, or a staff.

class.priest.why: Ruled 2026-08-27: one weapon — texts, symbol, or chain.

class.civilian.why: Ruled 2026-08-27: civilians draw no starting weapon and no starting armor. Their gear is dictated per unit (statBlocks kits).

class.beast.why: Ruled 2026-08-27: beasts draw nothing — their weapons are their bodies (natural rows).

heroKits._note: Per-hero overrides — dictated during the Eve differentiation pass, recorded in gen/eve-differentiation.json startingItems and mirrored here as the S12 registry. A hero listed here ignores its class kit. | 2026-08-27, the override grammar ruled with the start-kit rework: a plain ARRAY is a full kit — no randomness, the draw never runs (both elf rangers pin the Elfbow this way). {pinned:[...]} guarantees those items and lets the CLASS DRAW complete the rest — a pinned one-hander on a warrior or paladin still rolls the second hand; a pinned two-hander, or any pin on a one-weapon class, ends it. No entry at all = the plain class draw. One grammar, three cases. | 2026-08-27: a pinned ARMOR item satisfies the hero’s tier-0 armor draw the way a pinned weapon satisfies hands — the other draw still runs. | 2026-08-27b: ALL 24 Eve heroes now carry FULL kits (weapons AND one tier-0 armor each), dictated in the hero workbook — no Eve hero rolls the class draw. The class draws remain for generative heroes. The Serpent's "throwing dagger" resolved to Throwing Knives (the Skull took the Daggers pair, so the names cannot mean the same item). This resolves the two battle-2 blockers: Iron Dwarf (War Axe + Tower Shield + Destroyed Mail) and Battle Chaplain (Holy Texts + Knight Shield + Pilgrim's Habit). | 2026-08-27c, ruled: the Dwarven Brawler starts with NO weapons — armor only (Ragged Hides). He has the Brawler badge: +2 on brawl attacks, and the universal Punch IS his weapon. The buckler and whip are struck.

kits.civilianKitsLiveIn: gen/civilian-rulings.json statBlocks — same per-hero principle, dictated with their stat blocks.

armorDraw.rule: one random tier-0 armor per classed hero, from the armors whose startClasses cover the class; civilians and beasts draw none
armorDraw.source: Ruled 2026-08-27. The pools live on the armor rows as startClasses ("any" or a class list).

notPorted.why: It says 'only usable in melee' or 'only usable at range', which the TARGETING SHAPE already says — an ability aimed at 'one enemy in melee reach' is a melee ability by construction. Carrying it forward would give a compiler two sources for one fact and an opportunity to disagree with itself.
The weighted AI action table. HoBaT's AI modes live in engine/src/ai and choose their own way; a probability baked into content would compete with them.
A display name for an aura whose TIMING was cut with onEnter. The 14 are re-authored as spatial auras with their own names in gen/bestiary-riders.json.
Always the literal string 'enemy' or 'enemy-spell' — it distinguishes the two files this extractor already writes separately, and carries nothing once they are split.

notPorted.seenOn: all 412 cards, values foremost | backmost | random
notPorted.why: Lane placement in a three-column grid. A hex board has no lanes. The USEFUL half survives as `deploys: front | back | anywhere` - a Skeletal Archer really does want to start at the back - so the preference is kept and the lane is not.
Prose restating what the effects already say. Two sources for one fact is how a compiler ends up disagreeing with itself, which is the same reason `condition` is declined.

bestiaryCapabilities._note: Everything a row below needs that the engine does not have. All design-ruled in ENEMY-REVIEW.md 2026-08-23; none is an open question. A row naming one of these is complete content waiting on engine work, not a gap in the content.
bestiaryCapabilities.capability.power: The power pool. Integer; fractions resolve nearest, 0.5 up. Gained three ways (external pool / one-time on arrival / escalating clock or condition); consumers read it and mostly do not feed it.
bestiaryCapabilities.capability.inflict-affliction: Apply an affliction badge (possession | vampirism | lycanthropy | rotting-flesh — the family of exactly four) to a hero in combat. The badge swaps the hero's art to the affliction portrait already in art/heroes/<slug>/card/.
bestiaryCapabilities.capability.corpses: Corpse tokens as board objects. Created when any enemy is downed and when a hero actually dies (deathbed check → unconscious → bleed-out timer → corpse). Raising a corpse is summoning. One universal corpse art for heroes.
bestiaryCapabilities.capability.ground-layers: Poison and cursed as ground layers alongside burning and frost (same ask as Creeping Blight's 'blighted').
bestiaryCapabilities.capability.target-stamina-loss: The existing stamina loss, aimed at a target instead of paid as a cost. Same loss, normal recovery — one mechanism, new direction.
bestiaryCapabilities.capability.line-shape: A line area shape, plus 'furthest target in range' as a selector. Granted 2026-08-23.
bestiaryCapabilities.capability.enemy-action-cooldown: Cooldown/warmup on enemy actions — the fields hero powers already carry, reused.
bestiaryCapabilities.capability.giant-footprint: 3-hex footprint (one below, two above). No terrain movement costs; takes every affliction and trap on all tiles crossed. PARKED — not for a while.
bestiaryCapabilities.capability.stealth: A unit that cannot be targeted and does not appear on the map; moving onto its hex stops the move. Designed in COMBAT-DESIGN (Vision, darkness, fog and stealth) and never built. The Nightstalker re-enters it at End of Activation while standing on darkness, and rule.stealth-does-not-hold reveals one stealthed unit each Phase.

encounters._note: ENCOUNTERS — the P11 format, shaped by slice ruling 4 (2026-08-23): combat is simulated and toggleable, so an encounter collapses to a difficulty-ranked row with an enemy list. The full scripted form exists ONLY for the prologue battles, which are fixed by design and precede the map. Authored 2026-08-25 from ENEMY-REVIEW.md. FORMAT IS PROPOSED, NOT RULED — this is the sketch for review.

format.sliceRow: id · difficulty (an integer rank the battle list is sorted by) · enemies (unit ids with counts) · powerSources (optional: the battle's external pool and any scheduled gains) · terrainHint (optional). Nothing else — ruling 4 means no maps, no scripting for slice battles.
format.prologueBattle: The five fixed battles carry the full shape: setup (placed units by zone), schedule (phase-keyed spawns by edge), loseAfter, retreat, civilians, events. CLOCK RULING 2026-08-23: schedules count PHASES — the word turn never appears in encounter data. Placement is by hex — see format.placement.
format.powerSources: kind: external (pool at battle start) | arrival (one-time +X when a unit enters, stays in the pool after its death) | clock (per-phase or conditional gains live on the unit rows themselves — the Lieutenant's EOT, the Vampire Lord's kills).
format.placement: HEX PLACEMENT, ruled 2026-08-25 (zones were vagueries): at:{col,row} places on that hex; at:{near:{col,row},range:N} deploys anywhere within N of it; at:{oneOf:[{col,row},...]} is a scripted either/or. Board: 16×16, ruled 2026-08-25 — row 0 = enemy edge, row 15 = player edge. NOTE: engine/src/core/hex.ts still says WIDTH=HEIGHT=12; the engine constant needs updating by the engine session — the data leads. The old zone word is kept as `was` for provenance; the hex is authoritative. Multi-unit entries list one hex per unit in `hexes`.
format.scriptedEncounter: id · name · setup (units on the board at the start) · schedule (waves by PHASE, each naming units, counts and where they enter). A THIRD kind, first written 2026-09-02: it has a phase script like a prologue battle but is not one of the five, and it carries no hex placements because none were dictated — the sides are named in prose until it gets a board.

setup.was: mid — one right of centre, the 2026-08-25 nudge preserved on the 16x16 board

spawn.note: one Fast Zombie per side — four total; the old count:1 was per-side under the zone format

prologue.name: The Hunt
prologue.note: The first battle drawn from the battle list under difficulty — and the first affliction-inflicters beyond rotting flesh.

battleList._note: The difficulty-ranked slice rows, per ruling 4. NOT YET AUTHORED — battle 5 is the first drawn from here, and the list itself is authored once the P11 format above is approved. Shape: { id, difficulty, enemies: [{unit, count}], powerSources?: [{kind, value, phase?}] }.

civilians._note: Civilian objectives are FIXED HERO ROWS (class.civilian), referenced by id — no separate civilian unit type exists or is needed. Ruled 2026-08-25: Farmer, School Teacher and School Children are confirmed in place as civilian units. The dictated Lumberjack maps to hero.fixed.lumberjack-and-wife (the row that exists). ART: all six have legacy thumbnails in the Codex today; full art exists in hell-tcg New Art/hero-art/ as UNDECLARED v1/v2 pairs (farmer-family, farmer-group, lumberjack, orphan-child, school-child) plus settled schoolteacher and school-children files — picking v1 vs v2 is an art ruling per gen/art-conventions.json, not a guess, and local card/ folders for teacher/children are empty pending the art channel.

scripted.name: Horrors of the Night

schedule.note: nothing arrives — the quiet phase, and the one where the darkness the Eyeblights left does the work

scripted.intent: The board goes dark faster than the party can cross it. Four Eyeblights strip Vision from range 9 and each one that dies floods ten hexes with darkness — then the things that live in darkness arrive.
scripted.source: Dictated 2026-09-02. PHASE NUMBERING IS A READING: dictated as 'next phase ... in the second phase, or their first end phase, there is nothing ... the next one ... the next one', read as waves at the end of phases 1, 2 (empty), 3 and 4. Say so if the empty phase sits elsewhere. No hex placements were dictated beyond the last wave arriving from the opposite side.
